Action 1 — Start a fresh sales campaign for the hero product fgdSWla-. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: campaign.
  • Entity: new campaign "laxmisaree | Sales | Video 5 | 12/11", ABO (budget set per ad set), objective OUTCOME_SALES, purchase optimisation.
    • It is built fresh and is not a Meta duplicate. It is not a relaunch of 120250749814000052.
    • Ad set 1, "A+A | open | fb & Insta": copy 120250749814200052 as it is in Ads Manager. That is age 25–65+, female, open audience, with the same location rules and excluded cities (Aligarh, Amroha, Chakan, Giridih, Jammu, Murshidabad, Nadiad, Noida, Shahganj (Jaunpur Dist.)).
    • Ad set 2, "IB | interest | fb & Insta": copy 120250749813990052. That is age 25–65+, female, interest list as in that ad set.
    • The tool shows the NE-states-plus-Bihar list in an ambiguous geo field. The campaign did deliver to UP, Gujarat and Rajasthan. The Revenue member must open the source ad set and copy its location rules unchanged.
  • Change: ₹500/day per ad set, ₹1,000/day in total, started today (2026-11-12).
    • Ad: the "Video 5" video (source ads 120250749814070052 and 120250749814130052). Confirm in Ads Manager that its destination is fgdSWla-. The tool could not name its product.
    • Add both excluded custom audiences to both ad sets: users_contact_number_20260831_171107.csv and bad_customer_dump1_all_columns_20261009_133844_par. Only ad set 120250749813990052 excluded them before.
    • Make no budget edit for 72 hours.
  • Why: this answers root cause 1 (no sales vehicle) and root cause 7 (hero concentration).
    • The profit term moved is CPP. It was ₹453.91 in W44 against a break-even CPP (ex-GST) of ₹448.69. The target is ₹383.26, the W43–W44 blend ((19,544.53 + 17,248.41) ÷ (58 + 38)). That is ₹65.43 under break-even.
    • Status: campaign 120250749814000052 is PAUSED, with ₹0 spend in the last 3 days.
    • Over 8 weeks its S/GMV was 15.02% [2026-09-14..11-08 · get_campaign_level_data], which is 0.81× BE0 (18.56% [W44 · get_breakeven_sg]).
    • Ad level [2026-09-14..11-08 · get_ad_level_data]: ad 120250749814070052 had ₹38,221.48 spend and S/GMV 15.40%. Ad 120250749814130052 had ₹15,958.84 and 13.03%. Both are under BE0. These are on the Meta basis.
    • Hero break-even RTO is 59.05% at CPP ₹383.26, against settled RTO of 53.85% [settled 4 weeks · get_product_level_data_with_marketplace]. That is 5.20 points of room. At CPP ₹453.91 the break-even RTO is 53.43%, so the room disappears.
    • Under the tool's own rule (see Action 2) fgdSWla- passes at BE0 18.56%, but by only 1.96 points (directed S/GMV 16.6 [settled_4w 2026-09-28..10-25 · get_product_candidate_table]). That margin is fragile.
    • I departed from the "no relaunch within 14 days" rule only in form. The account has had no sales campaign for 12 days, and never leaving a gap outweighs a 2-day wait.
    • The rule for a Meta duplicate fails: the source has only one profitable settled week and two copies exist. So this is a fresh build.
    • The earlier copies failed on thin spend and budget swings. This one has flat budgets and a ₹2,000 gate per ad set.
  • Effect (hero m ₹1,555, RTO 53.85%, shipped per placed order 0.85):

| Case | Spend/week | Placed orders | Profit/week | |---|---|---|---| | Pass (CPP ₹383.26) | ₹7,000 | 18.26 | +₹1,410.15 | | Fail (gate at ₹4,000, CPP ₹766.52) | ₹4,000 | 5.22 | −₹1,957.10 | | Mid | ₹5,500 | 11.74 | −₹273.48 |

S/GMV is 16.05% (pass) and 32.10% (fail). The mid case of this row alone is slightly negative. It is the volume vehicle, and the plan total depends on Action 2.
  • Checkpoint: ₹2,000 per ad set. Judge Shopdeck S/GMV against 18.56% and Meta CPP against ₹448.69 (ex-GST).
    • Pass → hold for 72 hours, then +20% steps every 24–48h while under BE0, up to the seller cap (see Seller check).
    • Fail → pause that ad set and keep the other. If both fail, pause the campaign and go to the seller ask for a new product.
  • Seller check: the plan's planned budgets are ₹1,600/day, which fits the ₹1,500–2,000 combined band on Meta alone. Google spend is unknown. The seller must confirm Google spend, or that there is none. Cost price ₹730 (changed from ₹430 on 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-21) must be confirmed before launch.

, Action 2 — Test the next-best product fpxvt7rN_JzU in its own campaign. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: product and campaign.
  • Entity: new campaign "laxmisaree | Test | fpxvt7rN_JzU | 12/11". Product: fpxvt7rN_JzU (Women's Multicolor Floral Printed Designer Saree, ₹2,399).
  • Change: one ad set, same audience as Action 1 ad set 1 (open, women 25–65+, same exclusions and excluded custom audiences). ₹500/day.
    • Creative: a banner built from the product's 6 catalogue images, positions 0 and 1 first.
    • If Ads Manager shows which earlier ad promoted this product, reuse that ad. It ran in 120250749814000052 (₹1,207.9 spend, 16 orders) and in 120251160953160052. The ad tool failed, so no ad could be tied to the product.
    • The product has no UGC video (hygiene ask). The angle is the one the working "Video 5" uses. I could not read that video, so the Revenue member should write down what it shows before building the banner.
  • Why: root cause 7 says the account relies on one product. This product earns best after RTO: settled profit 33.59% on 20 directed orders, directed spend ₹3,473, CPP ₹173.65 (3,473 ÷ 20) [settled_4w 2026-09-28..10-25 · get_product_candidate_table].
    • The tool's rule is: eligible = directed spend ≥ ₹500 AND ≥ 3 directed orders AND directed S/GMV < BE0 AND profit > 0 AND in stock [get_product_candidate_table].
    • The tool prints "eligible: no", reason "BE0 not available", on every row. Its stated reason is "no settled week with ≥ 20 orders; same BE0 as the campaign decision table". The tool takes no arguments, so a BE0 cannot be passed to it.
    • I applied its rule by hand in python_sandbox with BE0 18.56% [W44 · get_breakeven_sg] and with 20.25% [W43 · get_breakeven_sg]. Every condition passes at both values:

| Condition | fpxvt7rN_JzU | fgdSWla- | |---|---|---| | Directed spend ≥ ₹500 | ₹3,473: pass | ₹39,222: pass | | Directed orders ≥ 3 | 20: pass | 95: pass | | Directed S/GMV < 18.56 | 7.3: pass (11.26 points of margin) | 16.6: pass (1.96 points) | | Directed S/GMV < 20.25 | 7.3: pass (12.95 points) | 16.6: pass (3.65 points) | | Profit > 0 | 33.6%: pass | 14.1%: pass | | In stock | 106: pass | 131: pass |

- So the product is eligible under the tool's own rule, and it also meets the alternative bar of 10 or more settled directed orders. The tool's "no" comes from its missing BE0 only. - Its break-even CPP (ex-GST) is ₹376.34. Its break-even RTO is 73.29% at CPP ₹173.65 but 54.95% at ₹383.26. Its settled RTO is 55.56%. - Stock: 106 units [get_inventory_check]. The test changes one lever only (the product). - Status: not live. This is a new vehicle. The product is in a campaign the Hero action does not touch. - The 22.22% cancellation (8 of 36, seller-side 16.67%) is a risk, shown in the fail case.
  • Effect (test m ₹1,397, RTO 55.56%):

| Case | Spend/week | Placed orders | Profit/week | |---|---|---|---| | Pass (CPP ₹173.65) | ₹3,500 | 20.16 | +₹4,820.70 | | Fail (gate at ₹2,000, CPP ₹766.52) | ₹2,000 | 2.61 | −₹1,201.30 | | Mid | ₹2,750 | 11.39 | +₹1,809.70 |

If the CPP is ₹383.26 for the full ₹3,500, the row is −₹74.56. That is the limit of the pass case. The pass case is 20 orders on ₹3,500. That order count rests on 20 earlier orders, so it is an upside, not the headline.
  • Checkpoint: ₹2,000 spend. Judge Meta CPP at or below ₹376.34 (ex-GST), with at least 3 orders.
    • Pass → hold 72 hours, then +20% steps while under BE0 and inside the seller cap.
    • Fail → pause, and ask the seller for a new product. No other row of the candidate table passes the rule: they fail on directed spend under ₹500, under 3 directed orders, or profit at or below 0. A_sVyvWD has 3 directed orders and ₹640 spend, but its directed S/GMV of 22.9% is above BE0 18.56%.
  • Seller check: confirm the ₹730 cost price on this product. Same spend-band confirmation as Action 1.

, Action 3 — Call COD orders before dispatch and call every failed-delivery (NDR) case. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: logistics.
  • Entity: all new COD orders from the two new campaigns, and the 3 open NDRs (Delhivery Surface, COD) [get_seller_ndr_summary]. The main courier is "sr delhivery surface" (132 AWBs [2026-09-14..11-08 · get_logistics_partner_data]).
  • Change: the seller team phones each new COD order before dispatch. It also calls each NDR case within 24 hours, starting with the 3 open ones.
  • Why: this is the RTO lever the gates allow.
    • NDR to delivered is 9.8% (10 of 102). Only 1 call was sent against 87 SMS and 87 WhatsApp messages.
    • First-attempt delivery (FAD) is 35.98% (59 of 164).
    • "Customer unavailable" NDRs recovered 7 of 23, so calls can save some. "OTP verified cancellation" (40.17% of RTOs) recovered 0 of 46, so it may not respond.
    • Each RTO point is worth ₹327.81/week at mid orders (s × 0.01 × (m + f) × orders, summed over both products). f is ₹181.94 (two forward legs of ₹90.97).
  • Effect: RTO moves from about 54–56% to 1–2 points lower. That is +₹327.81/week at mid (1 point) and +₹655.62/week at pass (2 points). The fail case assumes 0. The 1–2 points are my assumption (trial). The orders were already counted in Actions 1 and 2, so this row adds only the RTO term.
  • Checkpoint: after 20 shipped orders, compare FAD with 35.98% and NDR to delivered with 9.8%.
    • Pass → keep calling every order if NDR to delivered reaches 20% (my bar).
    • Fail → keep NDR calls only and drop pre-dispatch calls.
  • Seller check: no instruction conflict. The seller must provide the caller.

Action 1 — Put the partial-COD advance back to the standard ₹49. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: website (checkout)
  • Entity: the store's partial-COD setting. The live value is 15 percent, set on 2026-11-02 07:04:37 by the seller [get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs]. Earlier values were ₹99 fixed from 2026-09-14, and ₹49 fixed before that.
  • Change:
    • Set the partial-COD advance to fixed ₹49.
    • Do not change the default payment mode, push-for-online or the online discount.
    • Make no other payment or checkout change for 7 days.
  • Why: RC1, through RC1a and RC1c. The seller raised the advance twice, and the funnel stepped down after each change.
    • ₹49 → ₹99 on 2026-09-14: S/GMV rose from 32.89% (W37) to 55.05% (W38). Charged ÷ landing was 3.97% in W38 [get_website_analytics].
    • ₹99 → 15% on 2026-11-02: payment screen ÷ buy-now fell from 49.47% (W44) to 43.48% (W45). Charged ÷ landing fell from 2.97% to 2.20%.
    • At the W43 AOV of ₹982.16, 15% is ₹147.32 [W43 · get_product_level_data_with_marketplace]. That is three times the standard.
    • Account funnel: C2PR 5.46% → 2.91% → 1.83%. CTR rose from 2.53% to 2.75% [2026-06-15..06-28, 2026-09-14..11-08, W45 · get_campaign_performance_metrics]. Buyers click and do not buy.
    • RTO does not bind. Settled RTO is 14.34% [W38–W45 · get_state_level_data], against peers' 37.57% [2026-09-14..11-08 · get_seller_category_comparison]. A lower advance carries little RTO risk.
    • The diagnosis rates RC1a and RC1c as trial. Both steps sit on the change dates. The revert is the cheapest and most reversible lever.
    • Expected ₹5,364.21/week at full step: 1.18 × (0.49 − 0.33) × ₹28,973.50. The input is the average GMV of W38–W39 [get_product_level_data_with_marketplace]. The diagnosis ties RC1a to the loss, so the revert counts at that figure.
  • Checkpoint: read at day 3 and day 7 after the edit. Judge payment screen ÷ buy-now against 49.47%. Judge charged ÷ payment screen against 44.68%. Guard: FAD of the new orders at 65.82% or more. 65.82% is the Relaunch FAD [2026-09-14..11-08 · get_fad_by_segment]. Account FAD is unknown. The new cells add landing traffic, so judge the ratios, not the counts.
    • pass → both ratios at or above the line: keep ₹49.
    • fail → ratios still under the line at day 7: keep ₹49 and ask the seller for a checkout A/B test at the payment step.
    • fail → FAD under 65.82%: ask the seller to review the COD mix with the team.
  • Seller check: the seller made both changes, so the seller must approve. No standing instruction blocks it.

Action 1 — Turn COD off in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, West Bengal and Rajasthan. |DETAILS|
  • Domain: website (advanced payment rules).
  • Entity: the Shopdeck payment rules. Add one rule for each of the 4 states. West Bengal already has a rule that allows COD, so edit it. The other three are new. Each state is its own rule and can be reverted alone.
  • Change:
    • Allow online and partial COD only (COD off).
    • Partial-COD advance 10%, well under the 20%-of-AOV cap.
    • Refund on cancel: yes. Refund on RTO: no. This differs from the 9 existing state rules (refund on RTO yes). The advance is then lost if the buyer refuses delivery, which is the deterrent.

  • Why — ranking.

    • The states are ranked by ₹ loss after RTO, not by profit %. I computed a proxy: profit % × GMV × (1 − settled RTO) ÷ 8 weeks. It is not a tool value.
    • Break-even RTO per state is also computed. No tool prints it. get_state_slice_table returned "no active sales campaigns", and get_unit_economics, get_state_level_data and get_campaign_state_data have no such column. I used the unit-economics formula, r* = (m − a) ÷ (m + f). Here a is the state's ad cost per shipped order, spend × 1.18 ÷ shipped. Inputs, all 2026-09-14 to 2026-11-08 unless noted:
      • f = ₹99.79 per shipped order (₹4,191 shipping ÷ 42 shipped, W42 settled week [get_profit_with_settled_status]).
      • m, account basis = ₹388.50 = AOV ₹1,123.79 × (1 − 52.46% − 4.09%) − f (W42, the same row). This is the AOV of a low-priced week.
      • m, product basis = ₹625 (the Skywave value in get_unit_economics), nearer the ₹1,400–₹1,500 orders these states buy. P5y2ffo9's ₹604 gives a lower r*, and the verdict is the same.

    • Results (shipped counts, settled RTO, profit % from [get_state_level_data]):

      | State | Shipped | Settled RTO | Profit % | Proxy ₹/week | Break-even RTO, m = ₹388.50 | Break-even RTO, m = ₹625 | Payment rule today | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Punjab | 28 | 64.29% | −63.04% | −1,752.84 | −30.66% | 12.0% | yes (COD allowed) | | Uttar Pradesh | 120 | 61.67% | −16.75% | −1,609.27 | 24.84% | 49.4% | none | | Maharashtra | 126 | 57.14% | −11.87% | −1,319.04 | 22.51% | 47.9% | none | | Delhi | 66 | 56.06% | −18.55% | −976.98 | 12.42% | 41.0% | none | | West Bengal | 42 | 57.14% | −21.49% | −750.42 | 6.47% | 37.0% | yes (COD allowed) | | Rajasthan | 45 | 62.22% | −21.31% | −719.76 | 17.24% | 44.3% | none | | Madhya Pradesh | 35 | 62.86% | −16.65% | −444.52 | 20.14% | 46.3% | none | | Telangana | 40 | 55.00% | −9.80% | −375.59 | 18.11% | 44.9% | yes (COD allowed) |

    • Reading. On both margins every state above is over its own break-even RTO. At m = ₹388.50 so is Gujarat. At m = ₹625 Gujarat is the only state of the ten under it. Punjab's break-even RTO is negative on the account margin, because its ad cost per shipped order (₹538.19) is above the margin. The four chosen states pass the exclusion test (≥ 30 shipped, RTO above break-even RTO). The choice among them rests on ₹ loss, because break-even RTO does not separate the states.

    • Together the 4 states carry 304 of 1,004 orders, 30.28%. Their COD share is 91.45% (order-weighted). Their settled RTO is 59.71% (shipped-weighted). Both are computed.
    • Online RTO is 2.70% and COD RTO is 64.01% across the account. The comparison is an upper bound, because in-transit orders count as RTO [2026-09-14 to 11-08 · get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data].
    • Seller cancellation is 9.52% over the last 2 weeks, under the 25% gate [get_submetrics_data].
    • Why — history.
    • Delhi. The team asked on 10-16 to move Delhi and Gurgaon to online and partial COD only. It was closed on 10-19 under "Actions not possible (3)". The history gives no reason and no closer [get_account_history]. The new evidence is the settled loss above, −18.55% on 66 shipped, and RTO above its break-even RTO on both margins. The team is asked to give the reason (see Ops asks).
    • West Bengal. COD was disabled for it on 09-24. A team action of 10-01 re-enabled COD "if marketing performance does not improve" [get_account_history]. The data does not show the exact change. Its 8-week figure above includes the blocked week.
    • Why — payment mix. The largest order-share state, Maharashtra, is never put on COD-off (payment levers don't pay there).
    • Why — partial-COD RTO.
    • The store-wide partial-COD RTO of 11.11% (36 shipped, in-transit counted) was measured with no refund on RTO [2026-09-14 to 11-08 · get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data]. The no-refund-on-RTO setting here matches it.
    • The sample is small, so the bridge prices converted orders at a higher RTO in the fail and mid cases.
    • Effect (at relaunch volume, ₹7,000/week spend, per week):

    | Case | Orders lost | Profit ₹/week | Converted orders' RTO | Orders converted / lost | |---|---|---|---|---| | Fail | 2.30 | −281.47 | 25% | 10% / 40% | | Mid | 1.99 | +204.47 | 15% | 25% / 25% | | Pass | 1.15 | +1,191.50 | 11.11% | 40% / 10% |

    With ads off, the effect is close to ₹0. - Checkpoint: at the first 30 shipped orders from these four states after the rules are live, per state: - Pass → keep, and read the next state on the ranking (Punjab, once it has ≥ 30 shipped). Pass means: - lost-order share ≤ 25% - RTO of converted (partial-COD) orders ≤ 15% - seller cancellation under 25% - Fail → switch COD back on for that state. - Seller check: no instruction names payment rules. Tell the seller by WhatsApp first.

    • The budget binds: at ₹700, 7-day spend was ₹738.75/day, 105.54% of budget. Spend reached 80% of ₹700 on 6 of 7 days [2026-11-03..11-09 · get_meta_daily_performance]. Pause campaign 120249910762400296 (LAL | 12-10-2026). |DETAILS| Instruction: Pause campaign 120249910762400296 on ad account 1198385338829427 - do not delete it and do not cut the Rs.900/day budget Reasoning: Campaign 120249910762400296 has run three weeks at Rs900/day with S/GMV of 28.14% (W42), 20.13% (W43) and 29.24% (W44) against a 12.08% aligned target (get_seller_aligned_profit_and_sgmv) - gaps of 133%, 67% and 142%, all three weeks inside the >30% pause-and-progress band. It holds 100% of the account's Facebook spend (get_campaign_performance_metrics W44: Rs6,195.95, 42,596 impressions, CPM Rs145.46 vs Rs57.82 L2 benchmark, CTR 1.78% vs 2.014%, C2PR 4.35% vs 2.625%, frequency 1.268, type Creative) and is budget-capped: get_seller_target_vs_current_budget gives latest_daily_budget Rs900 and week_start_normal_budget Rs900, and get_campaign_rebalancing gives campaign_budget Rs900 with optimization_level CBO and spend_by_budget_perc_3d at 98.3% (Rs6,195.95 over 7 days on a Rs6,300 cap). There is no delivery slack to recover - only a new asset can change what the money buys. Config confirmed today by get_meta_campaign_settings: ACTIVE, CBO, daily_budget 900, LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, OUTCOME_SALES, ad_account_id 1198385338829427. The pause cascades to ad set 120249910762410296 and its four live PHOTO ads (Banner 1 120249910762390296, Banner 3 120249910869250296, Banner 4 120249910869260296, Banner 5 120249910869270296), all confirmed live by get_ad_level_data for 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01. The budget is deliberately NOT reduced - the spec requires the full Rs900/day to carry to the replacement campaign, and a token budget on a paused campaign would read as a cut., Create replacement Meta campaign at Rs900/day (open audience, 2 video ads). |DETAILS| Instruction: Create one open-audience Meta campaign on ad account 1198385338829427 at Rs.900/day with two video ads - EDU.PHONE and SPACE.BLUE - India minus Assam, Jammu and Kashmir and Bihar, age 18-65, all genders, facebook, instagram and threads, no ROAS floor. It goes live as soon as it is built. Reasoning: Route LAL_QUALITY is confirmed by get_campaign_routing_recommendation (route_reason 'HiRTO seller -> LAL on delivered-only, non-HiRTO category seed'), but the delivered-only seed the route depends on cannot be built from this account's delivered pool - see the seed-check action. The spec's own fallback applies: 'If it is not [large enough], do NOT build a lookalike: launch the replacement as an OPEN broad campaign instead (route OPEN), keeping the same Rs.900/day, the same two products, the same geo exclusions and the same bid settings.' That is exactly what is specified here. Geometry is copied from the live ad set per get_ad_product_creative_targeting: age_min 18, age_max 65, genders absent (all), publisher_platforms ['facebook','instagram','threads'], excluded_geo_locations regions Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar, geo_locations countries ['IN'], targeting_automation advantage_audience 0, optimization_goal OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS. The two products carry 96.3% of orders: get_campaign_product_data (2026-10-19 to 2026-11-01) gives EDU.PHONE 52 orders / 66.54% of spend and SPACE.BLUE 27 orders / 32.32%, while INT.BOOK took 1 order and SANK 0 - so neither is included. No roas_floor is set, leaving Meta on the uncapped lowest-cost bid, because the account has no reliable ratio to read a floor against and a floor would stop delivery. Budget: get_seller_target_vs_current_budget gives latest_daily_budget Rs900 and week_start_normal_budget Rs900 - the replacement inherits the full budget and account daily spend stays Rs900 -> Rs900, net delta Rs0. Both videos are new assets generated in this run (handles job_mYVCwEwe4Nyd and job_R5QuXGvUrD95), not the seller's UGC, and NOT the current image creatives - Banner 5's image at 1.58% CTR on 74.4% of spend is explicitly excluded., Confirm the delivered-only lookalike seed is too thin - ship open audience instead. |DETAILS| Instruction: Confirm the delivered-only seed pool before building the lookalike: EDU.PHONE 6 delivered plus SPACE.BLUE 5 delivered in 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-01 is about 11 buyers, so do not build a lookalike. Ship the replacement as the open-audience campaign instead, same Rs.900/day, same two products, same geo exclusions, same bid settings. Reasoning: This is the binding precondition on the campaign-rebuild bet, and it FAILS on the current data. get_campaign_product_data over 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-01 returns delivered = 6 for EDU.PHONE (snPRG9t2oVm8) and 5 for SPACE.BLUE (uzIlA3W2In5y) - about 11 delivered buyers over two weeks. The settled campaign window confirms the thinness: get_campaign_rebalancing_rto shows campaign_rto_perc 73.53% on awb_nc 34 with delivered 9. A pool of 11-12 profiles cannot seed a lookalike audience; the resulting audience either fails to build or models noise, which is why the spec names the OPEN fallback explicitly. The strategy's decision rule and its own conditional are followed here: the create action ships open_audience at the same Rs900/day, the same two products, the same geo exclusions and the same bid settings. Note what this costs the bet: the delivered-only-seed hypothesis - the mechanism the strategy identified for the Rs3,733/week CPM premium - is NOT being tested this week, only the creative change is. The account still holds the old lookalike_toys-and-games_20261005_6 seed (audience id 120249881618390296, built 2026-10-10 on 4,000 users from a 73.53%-RTO book); that audience must not be attached to the replacement campaign. Re-run this check once the W44 in-transit parcels land - if the delivered pool reaches a materially larger size by then, the delivered-only lookalike becomes the better route and should be built in place of the broad campaign., Ask seller for a daily NDR calling routine. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to start a daily NDR calling routine - call every failed-delivery parcel the same day it fails, and escalate any buyer who refuses to take the parcel - and to tell us who owns the calls and by what time each day Reasoning: This is the single largest lever on the account's dominant loss. get_seller_ndr_summary (days=30) reads: 63 NDRs raised against orders created 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-29, and the action counts are Calls sent 1 (positive 0), SMS sent 44 (positive 0, negative 0), WhatsApp sent 44 (positive 3, negative 0), Seller escalations 0, priority escalations 0. Of 46 resolved NDR shipments, 8 delivered and 38 went to RTO - a 17.4% NDR-to-delivered rate. The reason split is decisive about which failure mode this fixes: customer unavailable 15 shipments at 26.7% delivered, rejected by customer 13 at 0%, otp-based cancellation 7 at 0%, no attempt 5 at 60% delivered, delivery rescheduled 4 at 25%. So calls are the lever for customer-unavailable and no-attempt (26.7% and 60% of those shipments still get delivered), while rejected-by-customer and OTP cancellation are intent problems that a call cannot fix and that point at COD and targeting - which is why the payment-mode and creative changes are in the same plan. 17 shipments are still open and recoverable: 12 pending, 3 ofd, 1 rto_requested, 1 reattempt_requested, with 11 customer-unavailable and 2 no-attempt among them, and 8 of the 17 are only 0-1 days old. The ask is deliberately concrete (who calls, by what time, what happens to a buyer who says no) because the failure on record is that the routine does not exist, not that it is being done badly. This sits alongside the coupon and price changes because it does not touch the ad account - it is the highest-leverage thing in the plan and it needs the seller to act., Ask seller for the dispatch cut-off time and to keep the PPH queue clear. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to confirm the daily dispatch cut-off time and to keep orders out of post-purchase hold so NDR calls happen while the parcel is still recoverable - 1 order is currently in PPH beyond 3 days and 12 of the 17 open NDRs have not yet had a delivery attempt Reasoning: get_seller_ndr_summary section A shows 12 of 17 open NDR shipments still in 'pending' status with an average of 1.75 NDRs and 1.75 out-for-delivery attempts each - parcels where the courier has not yet attempted delivery, so the buyer's address and availability are still fixable. get_submetrics_data for 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 reads latest_pph_gt_3_days = 1, latest_pph_on_day_3 = 0, pph_greater_than_3 = 0.43 average and average_pph_on_day_3 = 0.14 - down from W43's 0.29 average and 1 latest, with o2s at 0.87 days and s2a at 3.75 days. The hygiene sweep independently flags 'Ask Seller to clear PPH' at 1 order in PPH for more than 2 days against a threshold of 0 (fetch_hygiene_actions, account_stage=hit, finding 1, impact high). The call and the dispatch queue are the same lever seen from two ends: a parcel still in PPH cannot be called about until it ships., Ask seller for an Xpressbees serviceability check before moving Delhivery volume. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to check that Xpressbees Surface reaches the pin codes where Delhivery Surface is currently failing - 10 of the 17 open failed deliveries are already on Xpressbees Surface - and to confirm whether they want Xpressbees Surface as the first-choice courier Reasoning: Item 13 of the work order. The evidence is real but narrow, so the ask is deliberately a serviceability check and a priority decision, not a bulk switch - which is also what keeps it from colliding with the COD-charge change in the same seller conversation. get_logistics_partner_data shows xpressbees surface at 54 awb_nc, FAD 23.08%, logistics_forward_spend Rs83.83 per order, and delhivery surface at 22 awb_nc, FAD 10.00%, Rs91.95 per order - Delhivery is worse on both first-attempt delivery and cost. But get_seller_ndr_summary section B shows the NDR picture is not clean enough to justify a unilateral switch: xpressbees surface resolved 29 shipments at 20.7% delivered (6 of 29) while delhivery surface resolved 15 at 13.3% (2 of 15) - a gap far smaller than the FAD gap, and delhivery surface still delivered 2 of 5 no-attempt shipments. Open NDRs split 10 xpressbees surface / 5 delhivery surface / 1 delhivery / 1 shadowfax, so the failure is spread across both partners. That is the signature of a pincode problem rather than a partner problem: 11 of 17 open NDRs are customer-unavailable, which is not a courier failure at all. So the correct ask is serviceability - does Xpressbees reach the pin codes where Delhivery is failing - before any volume moves. Note that the courier mix was changed by the seller on 2026-10-26 (get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs, courier_priority), so this is a live preference, not a settled one, and the seller may have a reason for the current split that is not in any instruction on record., Ask seller to widen the catalogue to 16-19 real SKUs. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to add 5 to 8 new real product variants - a different product, colour, pack size or age band, not a duplicate listing of the same item - taking the catalogue from 11 active SKUs to 16 to 19, and to confirm which four products are worth keeping Reasoning: Item 16 of the work order. get_seller_catalogue read today returns 11 live products with active_sku_count of 1 for each of the three hero SKUs - EDU.PHONE, SPACE.BLUE and EYuEiax8ozML - and get_product_details_by_product_id confirms sku_count 1 for both hero products with sizes '14.5 X 14.5 X 5 Cm' on SPACE.BLUE. A one-SKU product limits the breadth of the audience it can serve, and a deeper catalogue gives the newly rebuilt campaign more than two things to sell. The request is deliberately for real variants - different product, colour, pack size or age band - not duplicate listings, because duplicate listings split the catalogue's own history and make the performance read worse rather than better. The target of 16-19 active SKUs (5 to 8 additions on 11) is the range the strategy specified, and it is bounded on purpose: this account has 34 weekly orders and a 73.53% RTO, so a much larger catalogue would spread the same ad budget thinner and buy less learning per rupee. Item 17 is the read that tells the seller which four products to keep - it is asked in parallel and the two asks belong on the same call., Ask seller to hold seller-initiated cancellations below 3%. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to keep seller-initiated cancellations under 3% of weekly orders and to tell us the reason whenever they cancel an order - stock-out, address problem, or a courier refusal - so we can fix the cause Reasoning: Item 17 of the work order. The read is favourable but worth locking down: get_submetrics_data for 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 gives seller_side_cancellation_percentage 0% in W44 and seller_side_cancellation_l2w 6.02% over the trailing 14 days, while get_campaign_product_data for 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-01 shows SPACE.BLUE at 11.11% seller-cancelled across the window with 0% in W44 alone. A cancellation with no recorded reason is the one that cannot be diagnosed - get_cancellation_reason_data returns no reason codes for these products, which is exactly the signature that made an empty cancellation read look like a stock-out in the first version of this diagnosis. Asking for the reason on every seller cancellation turns the next stock-out or address problem from invisible into countable, and it is a zero-cost ask that also feeds the catalogue-depth ask (item 16) and the SPACE.BLUE stock watch (item 22). The 3% threshold is the strategy's and it is well above the current 0% W44 reading, so it asks the seller to protect a good position rather than fix a bad one., Ask seller to clear the one order in post-purchase hold. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the kidsbug seller to clear the one order sitting in post-purchase hold beyond 3 days today, and to keep orders moving out of post-purchase hold within the same day they are placed Reasoning: Item 21 of the work order, stated as its own ask rather than folded into the dispatch cut-off ask, because it is a specific today's action and the cut-off is a standing routine. get_submetrics_data for 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 reads latest_pph_gt_3_days = 1, latest_pph_on_day_3 = 0, average_pph_on_day_3 = 0.14 and pph_greater_than_3 = 0.43 - so exactly one order is more than three days into post-purchase hold, and the queue is otherwise nearly clear. fetch_hygiene_actions for this seller (account_stage=hit) independently raises 'Ask Seller to clear PPH' as a high-impact finding at 1 order in PPH for more than 2 days against a threshold of 0. The scale is deliberately modest in the wording: this is one order, and the point of the ask is to close the loop on it and keep the queue at zero, not to alarm the seller about a backlog the data does not show. The same PPH backlog is what makes an NDR call impossible - a parcel that has not shipped has no delivery attempt to call about., Cut EDU.PHONE price from Rs.599 to Rs.499. |DETAILS| Instruction: Update the selling price for EDU.PHONE (snPRG9t2oVm8) on kidsbug.com from Rs.599 to Rs.499 - a Rs.100 cut, 16.7% Reasoning: The seller raised this price on 2026-10-18 from Rs449 to Rs599 (get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs, 10:00:14, by seller Krupesh Patel, product share 66.1% of orders), and the economics moved as a price rise predicts: EDU.PHONE orders fell 29 to 23 (-21%) while its spend rose 21% from Rs3,679 to Rs4,609 and its S/GMV rose from 21.22% to 33.53% (get_campaign_product_data, W43 to W44). The ad kept buying; the higher price bought fewer buyers. EDU.PHONE carries 66.54% of account spend and 62.65% of orders, so moving it 16.7% down moves the majority of the book's economics. Price reference: 10 comparables with proven demand priced Rs215-Rs450, median Rs268 - the seller's Rs599 is 124% above the median and 33% above the best-rated comparable (Rs450, 359 lifetime ratings, 3.7 stars, https://www.flipkart.com/yuiop-educational-rechargeable-phone-musical-toy-28-functions-english-hindi/p/itm), and the highest-volume Amazon listing sits at Rs355 with 624 ratings (https://www.amazon.in/Kids-Phones-Mobile-Phones/b?ie=UTF8&node=1378298031). COGS is not the constraint: get_l3_l4_sg_rto_cogs_profit shows account COGS 24.05% of NMV vs a 41.41% org benchmark for W44, and get_l2_l4_aov_cogs_and_pricing shows seller_cp Rs150 vs org_cp Rs150.83 in the phones 300-600 bucket - confirmed again today by get_inventory_check at cost_price 150, stock 927, selling_price 599. Arithmetic: the cut is Rs100, 16.69% of Rs599, inside the 25% cap (floor Rs449.25); gross margin moves from 74.96% to 69.94%, still far above the org COGS benchmark. Break-even conversion lift to hold GMV flat at Rs499 is 1.20x (+20.0%). Preconditions confirmed today: is_active true, is_visible true, stock 927 units against 23 last-7d orders., Cut SPACE.BLUE price from Rs.699 to Rs.549. |DETAILS| Instruction: Update the selling price for SPACE.BLUE (uzIlA3W2In5y) on kidsbug.com from Rs.699 to Rs.549 - a Rs.150 cut, 21.5% Reasoning: The seller raised this price on 2026-10-18 from Rs599 to Rs699 (get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs, 10:01:01, product share 30.7% of orders) and SPACE.BLUE orders fell 18 to 9 (-50%) with S/GMV moving 20.29% to 23.42% (get_campaign_product_data, W43 to W44). At Rs699 the seller is 173% above its own proven marketplace comparator of Rs256 (top listing, 322 lifetime ratings, 3.6 stars, from get_product_level_data_with_marketplace and get_marketplace_demand_validation, whose comparator row for _c-2cV8PJGjP shows Rs360.13 against a Rs256 comparator - already in Uncompetitive territory at 141% of comparator). Rs549 brings the price to 214% of the comparator while keeping 72.7% gross margin. Break-even conversion lift to hold GMV flat at Rs549 is 1.27x (+27.3%). Preconditions confirmed today: is_active true, is_visible true, 969 units in stock against 9 last-7d orders. Note the second decision in the same window: the strategy deliberately did NOT chase the Rs256 comparator median - this account's buyer is impulse/COD rather than a comparison shopper, and a move that far would gut the book., Two new video creatives for EDU.PHONE and SPACE.BLUE. |DETAILS| Instruction: Two new 9:16 Instagram Reel videos have been rendered for the replacement campaign - EDU.PHONE handle job_mYVCwEwe4Nyd and SPACE.BLUE handle job_R5QuXGvUrD95. Do not reuse Banner 5's existing image as a fallback; it runs at 1.58% CTR on 74.4% of spend. Reasoning: All four live ads on campaign 120249910762400296 are PHOTO with no video_id (get_ad_product_creative_targeting: raw_object_type PHOTO for Banner 1, 3, 4 and 5), and campaign CTR is 1.78% against the 2.014% toys-and-games L2 benchmark, with Banner 5 at 1.58% on 74.4% of spend (get_ad_level_data, W44). Do not create price-change tasks for any of these three — they are parked products, not launch products., Turn off the checkout 'push for online payments' prompt. |DETAILS| Instruction: Set the storefront checkout setting 'push for online payments' to False on motiwalafashion.com, leaving payment modes as cod,online,partial-cod with cod first, and leaving COD fee, delivery fee and the online discount cap at their current values Reasoning: get_seller_website_checkout_config returns push_for_online_payments: True on a storefront whose settings_payment_mode is 'cod,online,partial-cod' with cod as the default, whose catalogue runs Rs.799-1,699 (impulse band, where a payment-screen prompt costs conversions), and which is spending Rs.0 today — so there is no prepaid-share effect to protect from turning it off. All five creatives were rendered in this run, one handle per product, and no handle is shared between two ads., Ask seller to source cheaper on Organic Honey and Sidr Honey, approve a coupon ladder, and collect reviews. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller three things: (1) renegotiate cost price on shopify_46577241227484 (Organic Honey, cost Rs.195) and shopify_46846869995740 (Sidr Honey 500 Gm, cost Rs.280); (2) approve generic coupons with minimum order values around Rs.1,099 and Rs.1,649; (3) collect and publish genuine customer reviews for the 5 launch products Reasoning: Three separate gaps, each with a number behind it. Launch one Open Audience campaign at Rs 1,000/day with 5 video ads. |DETAILS| Instruction: Start one new Meta campaign 'Blumen | Open Audience | Launch | Oct 2026' on ad account 1435724935109307 at Rs 1,000/day, one ad set (women, all India, Facebook + Instagram), with 5 video ads at Rs 200/day each sending traffic to their own product pages. Reasoning: The account has never advertised: get_meta_campaign_settings returns no Meta campaigns and get_seller_active_adsets returns no active ad sets (read this run), and get_seller_account_age reports never recorded marketing spend. There is nothing to pause, rebalance or retarget, so the campaign lever is open only as a start. One campaign rather than two, because two cold starts would split the launch budget so neither accumulates enough delivery to learn from. Rs 1,000/day is the standard first-campaign budget for a new account, and the account's daily budget before this is Rs 0, so the net change is +Rs 1,000/day. Open Audience is the first progression stage because a pre-live account with no customer file cannot build a Lookalike seed; get_campaign_routing_recommendation returned no route row for this seller (NOT CHECKED), so the type is chosen from the evidence. No roas_floor is set because the pixel has never recorded a purchase, so a floor would bid against a return it has no signal for and the campaign would read as dead rather than as a floor set too high; the campaign bids uncapped and a floor goes on once the account has a ratio of its own. The seller config confirms ad account 1435724935109307. All five products were verified live, visible and in stock (10 units each) with cost prices present and at least three catalogue images each. On targeting: the spec asked for women AND 18-65 while also saying not to narrow on both at once; Meta accepts one narrowing lever on a new campaign, so gender is kept (the entire catalogue is 'For Women' jewellery and the L2 shape runs women-only) and the explicit age band is dropped, leaving Meta's default 18-65 to let performance decide age later., Hold launch-set prices: no price change on the 5 launch products. |DETAILS| Instruction: Leave selling prices unchanged on all five launch products: VUh3iI74 Rs 1,699, yx0WoF9a Rs 1,499, TdO-L58w Rs 1,399, dmVx1LOj Rs 2,499 and 6MJx6QQz Rs 1,599. No price change on any of them this week. Reasoning: This is a deliberate hold, not a move. Cost is a fixed rupee amount and COGS is a percentage of selling price, so a price cut raises COGS% with no change in rupee cost - and on this catalogue it is profit, not the 25% cap, that binds. Rebuilt on a consistent per-100-placed-orders basis at the category inputs (RTO 30.02%, cancellation 14.95%, logistics Rs 79.34 per AWB, commission 15% of NMV, S/GMV 21.43%), every one of the 66 products goes profit-negative if cut 25%, and re-running across RTO 25-35%, cancellation 10-20% and commission 12-18% found no feasible price at a 25% cut for any launch product in any of those 27 combinations. For this product specifically, at Rs 1,699 with cost Rs 463 the COGS is 27.3% and the max affordable S/GMV is 30.4% against the 21.43% category target - it holds positive modelled profit. Cutting it to Rs 1,199 would lift COGS to 47.0%, above the 38.06% category benchmark, and flip profit negative. A price cut made before any demand data exists converts a thin margin into a loss with no signal to recover it, so the launch set is held at current prices and repriced from the seller's own data after week one., Ask the seller about the tsp_oR54 price, sourcing and Free Size display. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller three things: (1) Is the Rs 3,599 price on tsp_oR54 deliberate? At Rs 1,800 cost it runs 50.0% COGS, and only a cheaper cost price below Rs 1,800 (below Rs 1,370 to match the 38.06% category average) or a price above Rs 3,600 fixes it - a price cut makes COGS worse, so we will not discount it. (2) Can they ask recent buyers for reviews? Only 20% of our testimonials are under 45 days old and we want at least 50%. (3) Once a week of launch data gives us a real AOV, can we add a coupon ladder at roughly 2x and 3x AOV? Send all onboarding emails to rasikaggarwal23@gmail.com. Reasoning: These are seller decisions, not operator actions, and none of them touches spend. On tsp_oR54: it is the catalogue's most expensive SKU at Rs 3,599 with cost Rs 1,800, which is 50.0% COGS - above the 38.06% womens-accessories category benchmark and the single item fetch_hygiene_actions flags ('Update all visible SKUs to have cogs less than 50%', naming ygPohT6c / tsp_oR54). It is also the only product where a price move was contemplated, and the arithmetic rules the cut out: COGS is a percentage of selling price over a fixed rupee cost, so cutting price raises COGS%, and at Rs 2,699 this SKU's COGS rises from 50.0% to 66.7% while its max affordable S/GMV falls from 18.9% to 8.4%. Two routes clear it instead - cut cost below Rs 1,800 at the current price, or below Rs 1,370 to reach the 38.06% benchmark (a Rs 430 sourcing reduction), or hold the price and raise it above Rs 3,600 (Rs 3,999 gives 45.0% COGS). Raising is not recommended because this SKU has zero orders, zero demand data, and no marketplace comparator (get_product_marketplace_pricing returned 'No significant products found' and get_internal_pricing_similarity returned no image matches), so there is no figure to support a higher price. The strategy's stated price cut is therefore not carried out as specified; it is reported to the seller as a sourcing and positioning question instead, and this product is off the launch set, so no launch dependency exists either way. On testimonials: get_seller_testimonial_coverage confirms every product is covered and none is stale, while hygiene separately reports only 20.0% are under 45 days old against a 50% target - fresh reviews need real customers, so this cannot be an operator action. On the coupon ladder: aov_for_coupon_check is null and active_generic_coupon_count is 0 because no prior complete week exists, so correct bands (roughly 2x and 3x AOV) cannot be set today and a guessed band would discount the wrong order value - this is a week-two item. Also carried here: the hygiene item 'Free/Standard size SKUs should be displayed size as Free Size / Standard Size', which names the same product short id ygPohT6c; its catalogue size is currently 'Free Size' and should display as 'Free Size / Standard Size'. The standing instruction on record is that onboarding emails go to rasikaggarwal23@gmail.com, which is why it is stated in the ask.

Budget is campaign-level CBO at Rs 1,000/day for a seven-day Rs 7,000 test, uncapped lowest-cost bidding (no roas_floor, no cost cap) because the account has no ratio of its own to anchor a floor on and a floor would starve delivery. Seller instructions were NOT CHECKED for this run, so treat the absence of objection as unconfirmed rather than as agreement., Verify Meta Pixel and CAPI purchase events fire before launching the campaign. |DETAILS| Instruction: Before the launch campaign starts spending, open Meta Events Manager for the Pixel on superelevengeo.in and confirm the Purchase event is firing with value and currency on a real test order, and check it also arrives via Conversions API. The campaign is purchase-optimised, so if the Purchase event is not firing with a value, Meta has no signal to optimise against and the seven-day Rs 7,000 test produces a number nobody can read - it would look like a campaign failure when the fault is tracking.
